correctness.rationale: For the split square-zero local algebra, the squaring map has coordinate span \(W=\operatorname{span}\{x_0^2,x_0x_1,\ldots,x_0x_r\}\). An explicit \(2r+1\)-square decomposition gives the upper bound. In any decomposition, projection to \(\operatorname{Sym}^2(V^*)\) has kernel containing the \(r+1\)-dimensional space \(W\); the mixed terms force the projected linear parts to span \(V^*\), hence at least \(r\) independent projected squares. Therefore the rank is at least \(2r+1\). The unital Waring-rank/evolution-dimension bridge in arXiv:2609.32784v1 then gives the claimed minimal evolution dimension. Alder--Strassen supplies an independent matching lower-bound check.

value.rationale: Split local algebras with square-zero radical are a canonical and ubiquitous class of first-order local commutative algebras. The claim gives a complete exact invariant for the whole family, for every radical dimension and every field of characteristic different from \(2\), with a sharp linear formula and no field-size hypothesis. This is a natural substantive application of the new evolution-envelope framework rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
